title: Reducing 'I want to die' to a simple label
description: An abstract ethical-language case: a third party compresses a person's grave statement ('I want to die') into a simple interpretation ('he just wants to die'), without examining the fuller meaning-field -- pain, fear, loss of dignity, social pressure, coercion, alternatives, or a request for recognition. This is treated purely as a question about language and the will, not as a medical or legal matter.
intended_goal: Act on a single, simple reading of the statement.
expected_consequences: An irreversible interpretation is acted upon while the person's fuller meaning is unexamined.

language_act.text: He just wants to die. It's nothing, really; there's no need to look any closer.
